items.title: Another ‘signature park’ could be in the works for City Centre in Mississauga
items.summary: The city is laying the groundwork for what it says could be another “signature park” in Mississauga’s downtown core. Already home to Kariya Park, the tranquil Japanese-style greenspace named for Mississauga’s sister city in Japan, the City Centre area might also boast in the near future another park that would be “a distinctive and memorable public space that serves as a focal point for residents and visitors and has the potential to become a signature park within the Downtown Core,” City of Mississauga senior staff said in a report coming to council on Tuesday. In fact, if the plan comes to fruition, the new park would be located just steps north of Kariya Park at the corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Kariya Drive (see map below). But at just under one acre in size, the new greenspace would be significantly smaller than Kariya Park. In the conclusion of his report, Raj Sheth, the City of Mississauga’s commissioner of community services, said “the new park’s close proximity to Kariya Park, which is recognized as one of the city’s treasured public spaces, provides an opportunity to complement and enhance the broader park experience in this area of the Downtown Core. ” Staff are recommending the city enter into a memorandum of understanding with developer Camrost Felcor “for the purpose of exploring enhanced park design for city-owned property” at the southwest corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Kariya Drive. The greenspace is adjacent to the site being developed by Camrost Felcor.

items.title: Changes set for waste collection in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Fall is here, and that means weekly yard waste pick-up is about to begin in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon. Weekly yard waste pick-up starts the week of Sept. m. on your pickup day. You can check the collection calendar to find your pickup day, or sign up to receive free waste collection reminders. Starting in October of next year, the City of Brampton will take over garbage, organics, and yard waste collection in both Brampton and Caledon as the two municipalities prepare to take over a service traditionally handled by the Region of Peel. The change is part of the province’s broader restructuring of services in Peel Region, which is shifting several responsibilities from the regional government to Brampton, Caledon and Mississauga. Acceptable yard waste includes leaves, yard rakings with debris, tree trimmings and branches, brush and hedge trimmings, household and garden plants, and Halloween pumpkins (without the candle). Yard waste can also be brought to Community Recycling Centres, but the region notes that grass clippings are not accepted at the curb or at recycling centres. All yard waste at the curb must be in kraft paper bags, or reusable containers clearly labelled ‘yard waste’ with a sticker or marker. Plastic bags not accepted.

items.title: House of the week: Renovated home with pool and multiple fireplaces in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: Luxury Lorne Park home with a pool and multiple fireplaces. Features: This Lorne Park home offers over 7,000 square feet of living space and has been updated with an extensive permitted, architect-designed renovation completed in 2024. The main level features hardwood flooring, multiple fireplaces and a kitchen showcasing granite surfaces, Wolf appliances, Sub-Zero refrigeration and a Miele dishwasher, complemented by a servery with an additional Miele dishwasher and under-counter bar refrigerator. There is also a pantry/laundry area and office with a custom walnut workstation on the main floor. Upstairs, select bedrooms feature motorized Hunter Douglas PowerView shades and heated bathroom floors. The basement features radiant-heated Italian tile, eight-foot Kolbe doors, a glass-enclosed walnut wine cellar, a refreshment bar, a dedicated fitness studio, a purpose-built theatre, a fifth bedroom and a spa suite with sauna and rain shower. Outside, an approximately 1,000-square-foot elevated terrace and cedar gazebo overlook the pool and flow into covered entertaining spaces, stonework and an outdoor kitchen with leathered-granite counters, a gas barbecue, a cooktop and a sink. There’s also an outdoor gas fireplace, media feature and three overhead gas heaters. Two furnace and central air systems provide zoned comfort. Distributed audio, smart exterior systems, 14-camera surveillance, a standby generator, Kinetico water treatment and a fully-finished three-car garage complete the home.

items.title: Woman charged with murder after stabbing victim in Mississauga dies
items.summary: A Mississauga woman now faces a second-degree murder charge in connection with a Labour Day weekend stabbing after the victim died in hospital, police say. Peel Regional Police said officers who responded to a Sept. m. in the area of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East in Mississauga’s east end found a man suffering from a serious stab wound to the neck. He was transported to hospital in critical condition, but succumbed to his injuries four days later, police said on Friday, adding homicide investigators subsequently took over the case. The day after the stabbing, police arrested a woman and charged her with attempted murder. She was held in custody pending a bail hearing at that time, according to investigators. Peel Regional Police said on Friday the charges have since been upgraded. Lorena Sanchez, 42, of Mississauga, appeared again in Brampton court on Sept. 18, when the charge was upgraded to second-degree murder, police said. Anyone with information regarding this incident is asked to contact investigators with the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau at 905-453–2121, ext. 3205. Shortly after the Sept. 6 stabbing, police said the incident took place outside a shelter on Dundas Street, near Main Street, several blocks east of Dixie Road.

items.title: UPDATE: Victim Succumbs to Injuries following a Stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: Region of Peel – Investigators from the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau have upgraded the charges against a woman in connection with a stabbing in Mississauga. On Sunday, Sept. , officers responded to reports of a stabbing that occurred in the area of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East. Upon arrival, officers located an adult male suffering from a serious stab wound. He was transported to hospital in critical condition. The following day, 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga was arrested and charged with Attempted Murder. She was held in custody pending a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. On Sept. 10, the victim succumbed to his injuries and the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau took the carriage of this investigation. On Sept. 18, Sanchez was brought to the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton where her charges were upgraded to Second Degree Murder. items.title: Parrish takes heat from rivals for skipping mayoral debate in Mississauga
items.summary: As Mississauga’s four main mayoral candidates prepare to square off in the first debate of the election season Friday afternoon, three of them are slamming the incumbent for not taking part in another debate scheduled for early October. com in late July she planned to take part in only three debates in the run-up to the Oct. 26 municipal election. , will see the top four polling candidates present their plans for addressing key issues impacting the city’s business community. Four main rivals square off again next week Following Friday’s candidates’ event, which is being hosted by the Mississauga Board of Trade, the four mayoral rivals will get together on the debate stage again next Thursday night. The Oct. 1 debate is co-hosted by Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network. The final debate in which Parrish plans to participate takes place on Oct. 15 at Christ First United Church on Lakeshore Road West. It’s organized by the Town of Port Credit Association, Lakeview Ratepayers Association, Port Credit Legion and Port Credit Community Foundation. The other three main candidates are also confirmed for that debate.

items.title: Four Candidates, Including Three Newcomers, Vie for Mississauga's PDSB Trustee Seat in Wards 2 and 8
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, four candidates are running to represent Mississauga's Wards 2 and 8 on the Peel District School Board ahead of the October 26 municipal election. The paper identifies the candidates as Tamer Elkateb, Samantha Fung, Brad MacDonald and Michael Michalias. Mississauga.com's parent company, Metroland Media, sent each candidate a set of basic background questions as part of its election coverage, the paper says. The single trustee seat covers both Ward 2 and Ward 8, meaning whoever wins will represent students and families across both areas on the school board. Voters in those two wards will choose among the four candidates when they cast their ballots on Election Day, according to the paper.

items.title: City Hall Lights Up Orange as Mississauga Lines Up Library Talks, Museum Tours and a Flag Raising for Truth and Reconciliation Day
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Mississauga is hosting several gatherings and sessions ahead of the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on September 30, also known as Orange Shirt Day. City Hall will be lit in orange to mark the occasion, the paper reports. At the Hazel McCallion Central Library on Burnhamthorpe Road West, attendees can learn about the importance of Truth and Reconciliation through stories and shared reflection, with in-person enrolment available on a first-come, first-served basis and orange shirts encouraged. The Bradley Museum will offer tours every 30 minutes covering the history of Indigenous peoples in present-day Mississauga and the museum's ongoing work on the 94 Calls to Action, with free admission and walk-ins welcome, though reservations are recommended. At Celebration Square and the Civic Centre, the city will raise the flag of the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation to mark the day, followed that evening by an orange illumination of the Clock Tower. Digital screens at Celebration Square will also display the 94 Calls to Action, according to the paper.

items.title: MiWay Blames Visa Rule Changes and Manufacturing Job Losses for a Year-Over-Year Ridership Drop
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, MiWay has recorded a year-over-year decline in ridership, based on a new quarterly report presented to the city's transit advisory committee. City staff pointed to several factors behind the drop, including federal changes to international student visa rules, job losses in the manufacturing and warehousing sectors, higher youth unemployment, and net population losses across the province that have lowered daily travel demand. The paper reports that the ridership decline is also affecting the city's finances, based on a separate June 2026 financial report prepared for the same committee. Mississauga.com notes the figures were presented as part of the committee's regular review of transit performance and budget impacts. Staff did not attribute the decline to any single cause, instead describing it as the result of several factors converging at once, according to the paper.
